note: MADE-UP recall calibration set: invented cards (an invented kingdom, invented answers), no real source material and nothing about the student, so it is safe to commit. Copy it from tests/fixtures/ to data/calibration/ on the server and run: python -m app.calibrate data/calibration/recall_set_v1.json. Each case is a typed Revise recall checked with RECALL_MODEL in a temporary database. expect.points gives the accepted status(es) of each point; box_move uses the default thresholds (up at 60%, down under 30%); extras_include / extras_exclude name classes of 'other things you wrote' (on_card, in_notes, unverified, incorrect); incorrect_min is the least number of factually wrong statements.

cards.subject: history
cards.prompt: Describe how the Kingdom of Varn punished rebels.

sub.text: Their heads were displayed in public to warn others.

points.text: Villages that helped the rebels paid heavy fines.

examples: After the Hill Revolt, the leaders' heads were set on poles at the market gate.

cards.subject: science

points.text: A solvent is a substance that dissolves a solute to form a solution.

examples: Water is the solvent when sugar dissolves in tea.

cards.subject: science
cards.prompt: State three ways to make sugar dissolve faster in water.

points.text: Crush the sugar into smaller pieces.

sub.text: Smaller pieces have a larger surface area.

examples: A sugar cube dissolves more slowly than the same amount of loose sugar.

cards.subject: geography
cards.prompt: Explain why coastal towns have milder winters than inland towns.

points.text: Water heats up and cools down more slowly than land.
In winter the sea releases the heat it stored, so the air near the coast stays warmer.

examples: Seaside towns rarely see frost, while towns far from the sea often do.

cases.note: Paraphrase; heads on display is on the card
cases.answer: They executed the rebel leaders and put their heads on display in public.
Use hot water, stir it and break the sugar into tiny bits.

cases.note: A correct statement from the card's example line
cases.answer: After the Hill Revolt the leaders' heads were put on poles at the market gate.

cases.note: All three points in her own words
cases.answer: The leaders were killed and their heads shown in public. Families had their land taken away. Villages that helped them had to pay big fines.

cases.note: A definition needs its terms: the idea without them is at most partial
cases.answer: A solvent is the liquid that you mix other things into.

cases.note: A definition that uses the terms
cases.answer: A solvent is a substance that dissolves a solute to make a solution.

cases.note: Close to the terms but not quite
cases.answer: The part of a solution that does the dissolving, like water.

cases.note: Partial: the result without the reason
cases.answer: The sea is warmer in winter.

cases.note: Partial: too vague to be a point
Factually wrong: the opposite of the card
cases.answer: Putting the sugar in cold water makes it dissolve faster.

cases.note: True but on no card: a neutral note, no penalty
cases.answer: Stir it and use warm water. Sugar is made from sugar cane.

cases.note: Both points in her own words
cases.answer: Water takes a long time to heat up and cool down, so in winter the sea gives out its stored heat and keeps the coast warmer.
